summary: Piscataquis County, ME: steel tower moved to Barren Mountain in 1951, described in 1955 and staffed in 1965; FFLA lists it standing with the cab gone.

facts.design: Four steel legs, about 40 feet tall, with an eight-foot-square cab painted white (1955 survey description)
facts.status_note: Frame still stands but the cab is gone (FFLA asterisk; hiker site agrees); date of removal not found

access.note: The Appalachian Trail passes over the summit; no source says the tower itself is open to climbing

visit.trail_note: AT Access: Trail over the summit

events.note: Coast and Geodetic Survey placed benchmarks on the summit; no structures mentioned that year; the team likely built a 15-foot pole tower for its survey lines
Steel tower moved from Pleasant Pond Mountain to Barren Mountain
Coast and Geodetic Survey team described a Maine Forest Service lookout about 40 feet tall with an eight-foot-square cab
An Appalachian Trail hiker's journal records an active lookout man working that year

evidence.supports: 1941 Coast and Geodetic Survey benchmarks; no structures mentioned that year
evidence.quote: In 1941, a team from the Coast and Geodetic Survey visited the summit placing benchmarks. No mentions of any structures at that time.

evidence.supports: the same team likely built a 15-foot pole tower for its survey lines
evidence.quote: They did use (likely build) a 15-foot pole tower to make their survey lines.

evidence.supports: steel Pleasant Pond Mountain tower moved to Barren Mountain in 1951
evidence.quote: In 1951, the steel Pleasant Pond Mountain tower was moved to Barren Mountain.

evidence.supports: 1955 Coast and Geodetic Survey team described it as a Maine Forest Service lookout tower with four steel legs and an 8-foot square house on top, painted white
evidence.quote: In 1955, a team from the Coast and Geodetic Survey visited and described the tower as a Maine Forest Service lookout tower that is constructed of four steel legs with an 8 foot square house on top that is painted white, and about 40 feet in height.

evidence.supports: active lookout man in 1965 per AT hiker journal
evidence.quote: In 1965 there was an active lookout man working according to a AT hiker journal.
The tower is still standing but no cab.

evidence.supports: Appalachian Trail passes over the summit
evidence.quote: AT Access: Trail over the summit

evidence.supports: FFLA lists Barren Mountain as Tower Standing*
asterisk means structure stands with the cab no longer in place
evidence.quote: Towers that retain their structure and support with the cab no longer in place

evidence.supports: Forest Lookouts page places the tower in the Maine Forestry District

notes_for_editor: The build date and original builder are unknown. The 1951 move and the 1955 and 1965 details rest on one undated hiker-oriented site (willhiteweb.com); that site also gives the 1941 survey note, which the story paraphrases. The Forest Lookouts page gives only the county and agency. Current status rests on the FFLA asterisk and the hiker site. No Maine Forest Service records found. A search lead pointed to Maine Memory Network photos of Maine Forest Service towers, not checked. The record had no height; height_m 12.2 converts the 1955 'about 40 feet' description and is secondary.
